questions.question: Two Nation Theory.
questions.solution_html:
• Two Nation Theory: The political ideology that promoted the idea that the Hindus
  • and Muslims of India were two distinct groups with absolutely no cultural, social and
  • religious similarities- these two could not co-exist as a single nation -it ultimately led
  • to the partition of India.

questions.question: Tebhaga Movement
questions.solution_html:
• Tebhaga Movement: Significant peasant agitation in Bengal – 1946-47-the share
  • croppers (bargadars) demanded that the share of the landlords (jotedars) be reduced to
  • one third rather than giving half of their harvest to the land lords- demanded also-to
  • store the harvested crop in the godowns of bargadars before division and not in the
  • godowns the jotedars.

questions.solution_html:

questions.question: Analyse the concept of Homerule in relation with Annie besant and Tilak's policies
questions.solution_html:
• Analyse the concept of the Home rule Movement in relation with Annie Besant
  • and Tilak’s policies: First World War from 1914-1918 -influenced Freedom
  • Movement in India- denial of freedom to the subjugated people of the colonies was
  • criticised by the colonized population- Annie Besant entered into Indian politics- She
  • worked for the unity among the leaders of INC-she established the Home Rule
  • League in 1916 with the support of the leaders of INC-The Home Rule League started
  • its branches in different part of India- Motilal Nehru, Tej Bahadur Sapru, Muhammad
  • Ali Jinnah etc joined Home Rule League-she was imprisoned by the British-she
  • presided over the Calcutta session of the congress in December 1917-during the very
  • same period itself taking inspiration of Besant, Tilak also started the Home Rule
  • League- started working against foreign domination- He toured throughout the
  • country to carry the message of Home Rule Movement- Tilak was imprisoned in July
  • 1916-Home Rule Movement could enliven the de-spirited Congress-It had its
  • branches abroad also.

questions.question: Explain the working of the Constitution Drafting Committee.
questions.solution_html:
• came into existence on 29th August 1947- chaired by Dr. B.R Ambedkar- Review of
  • the draft- Integrated the resolutions passed by the Constituent Assembly- Committee
  • published its first draft on 21st February 1948- 114 days spent for debate over the
  • proposals of the drafting committee- the final constitution came into existence on 26th
  • January, 1950.

questions.question: Discuss the centralization of administration under the Charter Act of 1833.
questions.solution_html:

questions.question: Explain the movements in the Princely states during the 1930’s.
questions.solution_html:
• States Praja Mandals or States People’s Conferences were organized – these were
  • Mysore, Hyderabad, Baroda, Kathiawad etc. -December 1927 - the convening of the
  • All India States People’s Conference (AISPC) - attended by-700 political workers
  • from the States-the Government of India Act of 1935 projected a scheme of federation
  • in which the Indian States were to be brought into a direct constitutional relationship
  • with British India and the States were to send representatives to the Federal
  • Legislature- another supportive development was the assumption of office by the
  • Congress Ministries in the majority of the provinces in British India in 1937-Rajkot
  • Satyagraha-Hyderabad State Congress-protest against Nizam of Hyderbad- Popular
  • protests Travancore, Mysore and Odissa for constitutional reforms.
questions.final_answer: protests Travancore, Mysore and Odissa for constitutional reforms
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Critically analyse the methods and significance of the Swadeshi / . ]
questions.solution_html:
• Critically analyse the methods and significance of the Swadeshi Movement: Lord
  • Curzon and the Declaration of the Partition of Bengal in 1905-Swadeshi means of
  • one’s own country-economic resistance by boycotting of British goods and promoted
  • indigenous goods and articles- public bonfires of foreign goods- picketing of shops
  • selling foreign goods- propagation of national education- reviving traditional
  • handlooms and cottage industries- shift from moderate petition to demand swaraj
  • ground work for future Gandhian mass movements
questions.final_answer: ground work for future Gandhian mass movements
